2 · Paste the post copy

The state held two public meetings on a proposed 19,950 acre transfer to AIDEA near Houston and took no testimony at either.

The window on ADL 234762 is nearly shut. Written comment closes 5:00 p.m. Monday September 14th, 2026. Writing is the only way in. More than 2,000 comments have already arrived, by the department's own count.

Not one of the three state notices says data center. The furthest they go is "a multi-use industrial and energy development district". A draft classification order rides that deadline. About 15,100 acres would leave Forestry, Habitat and Water Resources for Settlement. Two conservation groups report it. No state notice does.

The state's own words on use, the classification order beneath them and the comment count.

Should the rest of the comment period argue the transfer or the reclassification underneath it?

#AlaskaLandUse #MatSuBorough #AIDEA

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Editor's note

The deck argues that the loud fight over whether this is a data center project is aimed at the smaller of two decisions closing on the same day. The conveyance of about 19,950 acres near Houston to AIDEA is the one being argued. The draft classification order moving about 15,100 acres out of Forestry, Habitat and Water Resources into Settlement is the one that outlives any tenant, and almost nobody is arguing it. The deck deliberately does not assert that the land is being taken for data centers. No state notice uses the phrase, AIDEA's plan lists it as a possibility and not a commitment, and slide 06 says exactly that. It also draws no parcel boundary, because the notices give acreage and townships and never a shape, which is why slide 08 carries EXTENT ONLY at hero size. The 15,100 acre figure and the at no cost framing are reported by Cook Inletkeeper and the Northern Alaska Environmental Center and are attributed on every slide that uses them. One thing to check before posting. The caption originally opened its second paragraph on ten days left, which was true at wake on September 4th, 2026 and went stale the moment the run crossed midnight, so the copywriter's catch was taken and the countdown is now anchored to the closing date rather than to a day count. It stays true whenever this is read. Worth a glance at the DNR notice page before posting all the same, since the deadline already moved once from August 19th, 2026.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post before 5:00 p.m. Monday September 14th, 2026, because the whole ask expires with the comment period. The strongest window left is a Tuesday to Thursday slot from 8 a.m. to 11 a.m. Alaska time, so September 8th, 9th or 10th.
  • Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, before the first reader arrives at a post with no citations under it.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes, hostile ones included, and keep replies to what the notices actually say.
  • When a commenter calls this a data center project, point at the record instead of agreeing. No state notice uses the phrase, and AIDEA's plan lists data centers as a possibility rather than a commitment.
  • Never repeat the 15,100 acre figure in a reply without naming Cook Inletkeeper and the Northern Alaska Environmental Center, since no state notice prints that number.
  • Check the DNR notice page for a third extension right before posting. The deadline already moved once from August 19th, 2026.
  • Send anyone asking how to comment to DNR's Division of Mining, Land and Water, which is where written comment on ADL 234762 and on the classification order goes.
  • Log saves, comments and shares at 48 hours, and note whether readers argued the classification order or only the transfer.
